::: {.why}
Week 2 told you queue position matters; today you measure what it is worth, which is the number that decides whether a passive strategy is viable for you at all.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report the fill probability of a passive order as a function of the size ahead of it in the queue.
- Convert that into the expected cost difference between a passive and an aggressive order, in basis points.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Estimate the fill curve: across many resting orders in your sample, report the probability of executing within a fixed horizon as a function of queue position, controlling roughly for the time of day. The curve will fall steeply, which is why queue position is the asset high-frequency firms compete for.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Turn it into money: an aggressive order pays the spread with certainty, a passive order saves the spread with the fill probability you measured and otherwise misses the trade. Compute the expected cost of each for a specific position in the queue, and find the queue position at which they are equal.
:::
:::
